items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Consequently Louis Jordan came up with tune called “Saturday Night Fish Fry” which was in reality what happened on Saturday night.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you something about this. You know you said the people really worked hard. And here’s one thing I thought about rhythm & blues. You know my father worked for a factory, Goodyear Tire & Rubber for 26 years. And when they work that hard, and they were able to save a little bit of money to have some fun on Saturday night, whoever the artist was that they were going to see, that artist had to make them feel like going back to work on Monday. Am I right?

You better believe it. Consequently Louis Jordan came up with tune called “Saturday Night Fish Fry” which was in reality what happened on Saturday night. And when they came out to the dances, as I said, it was something that they prepared for a long time before that. And what they did, not only did they dress up to come to those dances, but they also brought little boxes with food, you know, a little beverage wrapped in aluminum foil that they hid under the table, and some good fried chicken and some nice…
So in other words, you’re saying that the music was powerful in the fact that the artist was on the same plane with his audience. None of this superstar stuff like —
